shots.title: Define existing-event-store migration and replay authority

hazards.description: [architect review] Migration cutover lacked a durable physical write barrier against old processes.
[architect review] Legacy import lacked a deterministic total order and complete disposition rules.
[architect review] PostgreSQL global keys and unscoped foreign keys conflicted with project isolation.
[architect review] Finalization lacked explicit crash, abort, timeout, and recovery transitions.
[architect review] Custom stores could bypass the coordination authority contract.
[architect review] Migration barriers still depended on markers visible only to new processes.
[architect review] The import plan omitted server-assigned fields required for deterministic hashes.
[security review] Cutover did not physically stop legacy writers or constrain custom adapters.
[security review] Legacy import ordering was not a complete deterministic total order.
[security review] An already connected old process could still mutate during migration.
[security review] Import order ranked time before dependency class and omitted exact timestamp normalization.

shots.notes: Defined the existing event store as the sole execution ledger, with physical migration fencing, a complete canonical scorecard and event envelope, deterministic import, projection evolution, finalization recovery, and replay integrity.

shots.title: Define atomic append, idempotency, ordering, and integrity

hazards.description: [architect review] Canonical serialization and hash framing were underspecified.
[security review] Canonical serialization was too weak for portable integrity commitments.

shots.notes: Defined project-scoped idempotency, exact retry and payload-conflict behavior, gap-free ordering, transactional projection updates, schema evolution, canonical serialization, and chained integrity commitments.

shots.title: Define renewable leases, fencing, and recovery

hazards.description: [architect review] Atomic multi-resource lease grants were underspecified relative to one aggregate.
[architect review] External fencing did not cover overlapping unequal protected subjects.
[security review] PostgreSQL lease acquisition could race when a conflict-domain row was absent.

shots.notes: Defined authoritative database time, lease-request aggregates, atomic child leases, conflict-domain locks and token vectors, subject epochs, retry, requeue, dead-letter, escalation, and recovery policies.

shots.title: Define capability, privacy, retention, and adversarial enforcement

hazards.description: [architect review] Emergency redaction lacked a defined finalized-round lifecycle transition.
[architect review] Raw source hashes could disclose restricted legacy data.
[security review] Secret scanning covered payloads but not the complete caller request.
[security review] Cursor cryptography omitted a complete authenticated-encryption contract.
[security review] Redaction lacked separately authorized request, approval, and apply states.
[security review] Backup restore could reintroduce redacted data.
[security review] Cursor AES-GCM nonce uniqueness and issuance exhaustion were undefined.

shots.notes: Defined deny-by-default capabilities, trust bootstrap and delegation, classification-aware filtered views, complete-request secret scanning, cursor encryption, redaction authorization, retention, restore safety, and 49 hostile scenarios.

conditions.description: The contract governs concurrent multi-agent authority, durable migration, privacy, and recovery across SQLite, PostgreSQL, and custom adapters.

training.description: Coordination safety depends on one authoritative ledger, physical fencing, deterministic replay, and explicit capability and privacy boundaries.
training.outcome: The contract now gives S268 and S269 implementable invariants and hostile acceptance tests.

nutrition.description: 259 test files passed; 4,324 tests passed and 27 were skipped at exact contract commit 4082cbd.
TypeScript typecheck and the root plus pi-extension production build passed on Node 22.
The sprint tests, review provenance, and scorecard gates are persisted in SLOPE state.

bunker_locations: Install physical database barriers before migration inventory and drain pre-fence transactions.
Materialize complete canonical import envelopes before append and quarantine ambiguous legacy rows.
Lock durable conflict-domain rows before granting leases, including absent-resource cases.
Keep secret and redaction commitments classification-safe and reconcile restores against external deletion truth.
yardage_book_updates: Negotiate protocol versions and required capabilities before accepting a custom adapter.
Use RFC 8785 JCS with framed domain-separated integrity inputs.
Fence overlapping resource subjects with project grants and conflict-domain token vectors.
Bind encrypted cursors to principal, project, policy, query, visibility, expiry, and managed nonce state.
course_management_notes: S264.2 can define the human and agent collaboration workflow on these authority, privacy, and replay invariants.
S268 owns the minimum canonical schema and transactional finalization implementation; S269 owns leases and capability enforcement.
